result.title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
result.comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training on a small chemical reaction prediction task - a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用「数字锁柜」把加密神经网络嵌入宿主模型权重，构造仅在秘密触发器下解密执行的后门，并在化学反应预测代理任务上检验微调、权重加噪、梯度触发器搜索与 latent adversarial training 能否把隐藏能力诱导出来。
AI.relevance_reason: 属安全审计方向，与多模态推理无直接关系；但其 latent adversarial training 与「能力能否被诱导」的检验思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正承载并被因果使用，而非仅作为训练副产物。
